summary: A real but mild pain with a buildable $0 CLI, but demand is blog posts only, it is a free tool with no path to revenue, and it depends on a vendor-owned log format that Anthropic or Entire could replace. Not worth a demand-test slot.

demand.evidence: One blog post, one vendor guide and a feature-request issue; no user behavior, payments or requests. RESEARCH.md admits it is unverified how many run agents unattended.

statusQuo.evidence: git log, /resume and manual transcript reading; some users write their own JSONL parsers. Hook-based Entire and Semantica leave a retroactive zero-install gap.

specificity.evidence: Persona is a profile (solo dev running Claude Code overnight), not a named person. The consequence is a slower morning, not a career or revenue cost.

wedge.evidence: One npx command listing per-branch FAILED/retries/risky files, no setup. But it is a free OSS CLI with nothing to sell; the success metric is stars.

futureFit.evidence: More unattended runs raise the need, but the tool depends on an undocumented vendor JSONL schema and the platform owner or Entire can build the same view.

premises: Developers run agents unattended often enough to need triage (weakly supported by blogs only)
Heuristic receipts (exit codes, retries, risky paths) are trusted enough to act on
The Claude Code JSONL schema is stable enough to parse (unsupported)
Retroactive zero-install beats hook-based tracing (partly supported)
Someone will adopt or pay for a local CLI (not supported)
alternatives: Minimal: a shell script or Claude Code skill for personal use, no demand test
Extend RepoHQ with a last-night's-agent-runs panel, reusing David's stack and sharing log reading with pr-receipt
Ideal: ingest Entire/Semantica checkpoints as primary input with JSONL fallback (larger than a weekend)
wedge: npx dawnlog --since 12h on one repo, Claude Code only: one line per branch with matched session, FAILED/OK, retry count and a lockfile/migration/auth risk flag.

feasibility.notes: Node CLI, hand-rolled JSONL parser, git subprocess, regex redaction, Vitest fixtures; local-only, npm publish is free. Proof test: at least 9 of 10 of David's real overnight sessions attribute to the right branch. Expect parser fixes with each Claude Code release.

risks: JSONL schema drift breaks the parser
Anthropic or Entire/Semantica ship a morning view
No monetization path for a free CLI
killCriteria: Drop if the 2-week test gets under 50 visitors or under 5 signups, if no reader says they already parse session logs by hand, if Anthropic or Entire ship a morning view, or if attribution is under 90% on David's own runs.
